tier_justification: Tier 1: 7 work-units (agents/ roster, 3 fork-skill fixes, cite-check rename+move, dispatch rewiring across 5 skills, hooks.json async, description trim, docs) — above tier 0's single-work-unit predicate. No tier-2 predicate fires: no publish, deploy, migration, data deletion, or external send. HONEST DEVIATION FROM RULE 1 (freeze-before-build): this file is frozen AFTER implementation, at the request to merge an already-built PR. frozen_sha is the true freeze point (current head), not a backdated base. Consequence stated plainly: freeze-before-build's protection against evals written to fit the diff does NOT apply here, and rule 4 (oracle independence) is therefore load-bearing on its own — each assertion below is derived from the task's goal state as stated in the authorising prompts ('make coderails skills/agents/hooks efficient per the skills docs', 'no overlap with pr-review-toolkit', 'rename verify to cite-check because /verify is a built-in'), not from reading the implementation.

evals.assert: No skill or command instructs dispatch to a bare `general-purpose` subagent as the way to do work — every dispatch site names a concrete agent.
evals.cmd: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && ! grep -rn 'Subagent (general-purpose)' skills commands 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | grep .
evals.negative_control: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && printf 'Subagent (general-purpose): do a thing\n' > /tmp/ng_e1.md && ! grep -rn 'Subagent (general-purpose)' /tmp/ng_e1.md | grep .
evals.expected: cmd exits 0 (no dispatch-form matches remain); negative control exits non-zero, proving the grep can find the pattern when it is present.

evals.assert: Every skill declaring `context: fork` also declares an `agent:`, so no forked skill silently falls back to the untyped general-purpose default.
evals.cmd: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && bad=0; for f in $(grep -rl '^context: fork' skills */SKILL.md 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules); do grep -q '^agent:' "$f" || { echo "MISSING agent: $f"; bad=1; }; done; [ "$bad" -eq 0 ]
evals.negative_control:
d=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir -p "$d/skills/x" && printf -- '---
context: fork
---
' > "$d/skills/x/SKILL.md" && cd "$d" && bad=0; for f in $(grep -rl '^context: fork' skills 2>/dev/null); do grep -q '^agent:' "$f" || bad=1; done; [ "$bad" -eq 0 ]
evals.expected: cmd exits 0 (all fork skills carry agent:); negative control exits non-zero on a synthetic fork-skill lacking agent:, proving the loop detects the gap.

evals.assert: No file-writing forked skill runs in the background, where its edits would land outside session checkpoints and escape /rewind.
evals.cmd: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && for s in wiki-ingest wiki-query; do grep -q '^background: false' "skills/$s/SKILL.md" || { echo "NOT foreground: $s"; exit 1; }; done
evals.negative_control:
d=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir -p "$d/skills/wiki-ingest" && printf -- '---
context: fork
---
' > "$d/skills/wiki-ingest/SKILL.md" && cd "$d" && for s in wiki-ingest; do grep -q '^background: false' "skills/$s/SKILL.md" || exit 1; done
evals.expected: cmd exits 0; negative control exits non-zero against a synthetic fork-skill with no background: false line.

evals.assert: Every agent this repo ships parses as valid YAML frontmatter and declares only fields the plugin agent schema supports — hooks, mcpServers and permissionMode are rejected for plugin-shipped agents.
evals.cmd:
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && python3 -c "import re,glob,sys; bad=[]; [bad.append(f) for f in glob.glob('agents/*.md') if not re.match(r'^---
.*?
---
', open(f).read(), re.S)]; forb=[(f,k) for f in glob.glob('agents/*.md') for k in re.findall(r'^([a-z-]+):', re.match(r'^---
(.*?)
---', open(f).read(), re.S).group(1), re.M) if k in ('hooks','mcpServers','permissionMode')]; print('unparseable:',bad); print('forbidden:',forb); sys.exit(1 if bad or forb else 0)"
evals.negative_control:
d=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir -p "$d/agents" && printf -- '---
name: x
hooks:
  Stop: []
---
' > "$d/agents/x.md" && cd "$d" && python3 -c "import re,glob,sys; forb=[(f,k) for f in glob.glob('agents/*.md') for k in re.findall(r'^([a-z-]+):', re.match(r'^---
(.*?)
---', open(f).read(), re.S).group(1), re.M) if k in ('hooks','mcpServers','permissionMode')]; sys.exit(1 if forb else 0)"
evals.expected: cmd exits 0 (all agents parse, none use forbidden fields); negative control exits non-zero on a synthetic agent declaring hooks:.

evals.assert: The claim-auditing skill does not collide with Claude Code's bundled /verify skill: it is named cite-check, and no stale reference to the old name survives anywhere in the repo.
evals.cmd: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && test -f skills/cite-check/SKILL.md && grep -q '^name: cite-check' skills/cite-check/SKILL.md && test ! -e commands/verify.md && test ! -d skills/verify && ! grep -rn 'coderails:verify' README.md INSTALLATION.md docs skills commands 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | grep .
evals.negative_control: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && printf 'see /coderails:verify for details\n' > /tmp/ng_e5.md && ! grep -rn 'coderails:verify' /tmp/ng_e5.md | grep .
evals.expected: cmd exits 0 (renamed, old paths gone, zero stale refs); negative control exits non-zero, proving the stale-ref grep fires when a reference is present.

evals.assert: hooks.json remains valid JSON and the only cosmetic Stop hook is non-blocking, while every correctness-gating Stop hook still blocks.
evals.cmd: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('hooks/hooks.json')); st=d['hooks']['Stop'][0]['hooks']; va=[h for h in st if 'voice_announce' in h['command']]; others=[h for h in st if 'voice_announce' not in h['command']]; sys.exit(0 if len(va)==1 and va[0].get('async') is True and all(h.get('async') is not True for h in others) else 1)"
evals.negative_control: python3 -c "import json,sys,tempfile,os; d={'hooks':{'Stop':[{'hooks':[{'command':'voice_announce.sh'}]}]}}; p=tempfile.mktemp(); json.dump(d,open(p,'w')); e=json.load(open(p)); st=e['hooks']['Stop'][0]['hooks']; va=[h for h in st if 'voice_announce' in h['command']]; sys.exit(0 if len(va)==1 and va[0].get('async') is True else 1)"
evals.expected: cmd exits 0 (voice_announce async, no gating hook made async); negative control exits non-zero against a synthetic hooks.json where voice_announce lacks async.

evals.assert: The repo's own hook test suite passes in full on a clean checkout of the branch — no test was broken by the rewiring, and none silently disappeared.
evals.cmd: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && n=$(ls hooks/scripts/tests/*.test.sh | wc -l | tr -d ' ') && p=$(ls hooks/scripts/tests/*.test.sh | xargs -P 8 -I{} sh -c 'bash "{}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo PASS' | grep -c PASS) && echo "$p/$n" && [ "$p" = "$n" ]
evals.negative_control: d=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir -p "$d/t" && printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 1\n' > "$d/t/x.test.sh" && cd "$d" && n=$(ls t/*.test.sh | wc -l | tr -d ' ') && p=$(ls t/*.test.sh | xargs -P 2 -I{} sh -c 'bash "{}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo PASS' | grep -c PASS); [ "$p" = "$n" ]
evals.expected: cmd exits 0 and prints N/N; negative control exits non-zero against a deliberately failing test, proving the pass-count comparison discriminates.

evals.assert: coderails does not duplicate any agent already shipped by pr-review-toolkit, its declared dependency.
evals.cmd: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && for a in code-reviewer code-simplifier comment-analyzer pr-test-analyzer silent-failure-hunter type-design-analyzer; do test ! -e "agents/$a.md" || { echo "DUPLICATE: $a"; exit 1; }; done
evals.negative_control: d=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir -p "$d/agents" && touch "$d/agents/code-reviewer.md" && cd "$d" && for a in code-reviewer; do test ! -e "agents/$a.md" || exit 1; done
evals.expected: cmd exits 0 (no overlapping agent names); negative control exits non-zero when a duplicate is planted.

evals.assert: The new agents/ component type is documented for users, not shipped silently.
evals.cmd: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && grep -qi '^## Agents' README.md && grep -qi '^## Agents' docs/REFERENCE.md
evals.negative_control: d=$(mktemp -d) && printf '# Readme\nno agents section\n' > "$d/README.md" && cd "$d" && grep -qi '^## Agents' README.md
evals.expected: cmd exits 0 (both docs carry an Agents section); negative control exits non-zero against a README with no such section.
